mode: preseason dry-run (all 10 rosters still 0-0-0, waiver_budget_used still 0 leaguewide — this week's adds have processed as uncontested free-agent claims, not priced FAAB auctions, even on Sept 1's normal Tuesday cycle)
note: No material change to the pool since the Sept 2 correction: Coker, Shakir and Rodriguez are all still unclaimed, and Kayshon Boutte (104.7 projected) remains my only genuinely droppable bench piece (Odunze 173.9, Ferguson 124.8, Johnston 134.9, Washington 89.5-as-Jeanty's-handcuff all keepers). Only one real update moves the board today: Khalil Shakir has gotten WORSE, not better, since yesterday. He missed practice again Tuesday Sept 1 (undisclosed injury, out since Aug 20, sat both final preseason games), and while CBS Sports sources still frame Buffalo as cautiously optimistic for the Sept 13 opener at Houston, one Bills-beat headline today quotes coach Sean McDermott saying the injury is 'gonna take some time.' That's a real step down from yesterday's flat 'Questionable tag' framing, so Shakir drops behind Rodriguez in priority even though his box-score history is the best of the three. Rodriguez/Tuten remain a confirmed camp-committee with no clearer split (Liam Coen still says the touch count will be 'more by committee'), and my own Ashton Jeanty is STILL sidelined as of Wednesday Sept 2 with 11 days to the opener — no new action needed there since I already roster the direct handcuff, Mike Washington, but it's the single biggest injury watch on my own roster this week. Rival-need read unchanged: bwalsh89 still runs the league's thinnest RB bench (Skattebo, Harvey, Chase Brown) and is the one owner with structural reason to grab any Jaguars back on sight.

targets.why: Clear WR2 in Carolina opposite Tetairoa McMillan, backed by a three-year, 34-million-dollar extension signed in July 2026. From Week 8 of 2025 onward he played 73% of snaps with a 17.8% target share and topped 14 points in four of his final six games. No injury designation, unchanged and still the cleanest health profile of the three real options.
targets.asset: 135.9 projected points in HBGBs scoring (Sleeper season projections), the best combination of role certainty and health in the free-agent pool.
targets.my_team_impact: Doesn't crack my starting ten over Pickens/Egbuka/Odunze, but is a real upgrade on the WR6 bench spot: +31.2 over Boutte for the same roster slot, plus cover for the Week 10 bye that removes Egbuka, Odunze, Irving and the Eagles DEF at once.
targets.worth: FAAB 4-6 ceiling if the market were open.
targets.confidence_why: Role, contract and health are all cleanly reported, but zero 2026 regular-season snaps caps confidence below high no matter how clean the report reads.
targets.competition: mfkr and Sladsous both carry the league's least concentrated WR rooms and remain active on the wire.
targets.bid: Free-agent claim, FAAB waivers haven't opened
targets.drop: Kayshon Boutte (HOU), 104.7, role reads in_flux. Only one open bench spot: claim Coker OR Rodriguez OR Shakir, not more than one.

targets.why: Signed a two-year, 10-million-dollar deal with Jacksonville in March 2026 after Travis Etienne's departure. Confirmed camp co-starter alongside my own Bhayshul Tuten; coach Liam Coen still on record today saying the touch split 'is going to have to be a little bit more by committee,' with reporting through Sept 2 showing the two backs splitting first-team reps roughly evenly and no pecking order established two weeks from kickoff.
targets.asset: 125.0 projected points, the best available running back in the entire free-agent pool by a wide margin (next closest is Justice Hill at 55.7). No injury designation.
targets.my_team_impact: Doesn't start over Taylor/Jeanty/Irving/Tuten. The real case is correlation: I already own the other half of this committee, so adding Rodriguez captures Jacksonville RB production regardless of which back the coaches favor week to week, instead of leaving me fully exposed if touches tilt away from Tuten. Clears Boutte by +20.3 and now ranks ahead of Shakir given Shakir's worsening health situation below.
targets.worth: FAAB 5-8 ceiling if the market were open, a touch above the WR asks given RB scarcity and the hedge value, discounted for the still-unsettled touch split.
targets.confidence_why: The co-starter role is confirmed by multiple camp-depth-chart reports and real contract investment, not a one-week blip, but it's a genuine committee with zero regular-season snaps to confirm the split, which caps confidence below high.
targets.competition: bwalsh89 carries only three rostered running backs (Skattebo, Harvey, Chase Brown), the league's thinnest RB bench, and is the one owner with a structural reason to claim any decent free-agent back on sight.
targets.bid: Free-agent claim, FAAB waivers haven't opened
targets.drop: Kayshon Boutte (HOU). Same single open spot as Coker and Shakir; pick one of the three rather than stacking.

targets.why: Two straight top-40 finishes, WR36 in 2025 on 72-719-4, now Buffalo's WR2 following DJ Moore's arrival. WORSENED today: he missed Tuesday Sept 1 practice with the same undisclosed injury that has now kept him out since Aug 20 and sitting both of Buffalo's final two preseason games. CBS Sports still reports cautious optimism for the Sept 13 opener at Houston, but a separate Bills-beat piece today quotes coach Sean McDermott saying the injury is 'gonna take some time' — a real downgrade from yesterday's flat Questionable framing.
targets.asset: 135.2 projected points, the longest established production track record in this group, undercut by two full weeks of missed practice time heading into Week 1.
targets.my_team_impact: Same slot logic as Coker/Rodriguez: +30.5 on Boutte, bench depth and Week 10 bye cover, no path into my starting ten as currently built. A stash can absorb missed Week 1 snaps, but a real risk of landing on IR before ever suiting up would waste the claim on my 5-man bench.
targets.worth: FAAB 3-5 ceiling, trimmed down from yesterday's 4-6 given the added health risk.
targets.confidence_why: Deepest production history in the pool, but two full weeks without practice reps and a coach saying the recovery 'will take some time' is a real, still-unresolved availability risk, not just an unspecified tag — downgraded from med to low today.
targets.competition: Same WR-needy pair, mfkr and Sladsous, though neither has moved on him given the injury cloud.
targets.bid: Free-agent claim, FAAB waivers haven't opened
targets.drop: n/a at watch — revisit once he returns to practice or the Bills issue a real Week 1 game-status designation.

DiaperDutyDaddy dropped him from this league's roster Aug 31, choosing to keep Kyler Murray instead, in a room already running McLaurin/Moore/ASB/Addison at WR.

targets.worth: FAAB 3-5 ceiling, discounted off the raw projection for the target competition.
targets.confidence_why: The projection and the depth chart still disagree (RWR3 versus team target leader), and a rival just released him from a stacked room rather than a thin one, which doesn't resolve the ambiguity either way.
targets.competition: No rival is actively chasing a crowded-room WR3 this early.
targets.bid: Free-agent claim, FAAB waivers haven't opened
